name: Floor basics
description: Moves that work on any dance floor, to any beat. Start here. Danced to anything with a steady beat, usually around 110–130 BPM. Each move card has the cues and a beat to count along to: try it, then mark whether you could do it.

source.name: Written for Study Buddy as a casual primer.

questions.prompt: Knee bounce: how does it go?
answers: Soft knees that dip a little on each beat. Almost every other move sits on top of this.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft
On each beat, let your knees dip a few centimetres
Come back up between beats, but never lock your knees
Let your shoulders and head ride along with the bounce
questions.explanation: Feeling the beat in your knees is what makes the rest of your body look like it's dancing to the music rather than next to it. Tip: Find the kick drum first and bounce only on that. Tip: Smaller is cooler: a tiny bounce on time beats a big one off time.
questions.note: Watch out for: bouncing up on the beat instead of down; locking the knees between bounces, which makes it look stiff.

answers: Step to one side, bring the other foot in to tap, then go back the other way.
steps: Step your right foot out to the right (1)
Bring your left foot in and tap it next to the right (2)
Step your left foot out to the left (3)
Tap the right foot next to it (4)
questions.explanation: Tip: Keep the knee bounce going underneath. Tip: Once it's automatic, let your shoulders swing the opposite way to your feet.
questions.note: Watch out for: stepping too wide, which eats floor space and pulls you off the beat.

questions.prompt: Weight-shift sway: how does it go?
answers: Feet stay put while your weight rolls from one foot to the other, and the hips follow.
steps: Feet a bit wider than hip-width, knees soft
Shift your weight over the left foot on 1, so the right heel can lift
Shift over the right foot on 2
Let the hips and shoulders follow the weight, not lead it
questions.explanation: Tip: Try it at half speed (one shift every two beats) for slow tracks. Tip: This is the move to fall back on when you've lost the beat.
questions.note: Watch out for: swinging only the hips while the weight stays in the middle.

questions.prompt: Loose arms: how does it go?
answers: Give your hands somewhere to be: elbows bent, hands around waist to chest height, moving with the body.
steps: Bend your elbows and bring your hands up to between waist and chest
Loosen your fists, or make them soft
Let the hands rise and fall a little with the knee bounce
Every few bars, change it: one arm swings, or both hands push down on the beat
questions.explanation: Most people feel awkward because of their arms, not their feet. A default arm position takes that worry away. Tip: Watch the hands of someone whose dancing you like, then borrow one gesture.
questions.note: Watch out for: arms hanging straight down, which reads as 'not dancing'; arms flying wide on a crowded floor.

questions.prompt: Dancing in a crowd: how does it go?
answers: Keep your moves inside your own footprint, and go bigger only when there's space.
steps: Before you start, notice how much room you have around you
On a packed floor, keep feet under your hips and elbows in
Save spins, kicks and wide arms for when a gap opens
If you bump someone, a quick smile or hand on the heart is all it takes
questions.explanation: Being easy to dance next to is the fastest way to feel welcome on any floor. Tip: Face the DJ or the speakers when it's packed: everyone moves the same way and nobody collides.
questions.note: Watch out for: practising a big new move in the middle of a packed floor.
